title: Mean platelet volume does not improve cross-sample airflow-obstruction prediction beyond clinical and standard blood-count measures
abstract: A registered fixed ridge-logistic model fitted in NHANES2007–2008 (n=3542,513 cases) was transported to independently sampled NHANES2009–2010 (n=3968,521 cases). Adding mean platelet volume to demographics, smoking status, body size, platelet count, white count and hemoglobin changed prebronchodilator FEV1/FVC<0.70 discrimination from AUC0.788316 to 0.787870: difference-0.000445, paired conditional95% interval[-0.001515,0.000657], joint source/target-refit interval[-0.003515,0.000410]. Log loss worsened slightly. This negative incremental-prediction result does not establish equivalence, exclude platelet biology, diagnose COPD, or validate across healthcare systems.
